One platform for science tutoring and STEM activities.

SMARTinSCIENCE was set up by Rod Martin in 2026 to bring together his tutoring and STEM businesses into one platform. Rod has been teaching Science for over 20 years in England and continues to teach part-time in Leeds — focussing on Years 9 to 11.

Rod has a wealth of experience in curriculum design and teaching & learning. His positive attitude has supported thousands of children through their Science GCSEs, and because he still teaches part-time in Yorkshire he is very aware of how to support students through their science exams.

Three sciences, and the skills that carry the marks

Embedding exam technique within all lessons.

Biology

Chemistry

Physics

Working Scientifically

Two things worth knowing first

There is one National Science Curriculum in England & Wales and four exam boards examining it. Which board your child sits, and which course they are on, changes how they should revise.

Which exam board?

AQA, Edexcel, OCR or Eduqas. The content is the same, but each board organises it differently and writes its papers differently — so knowing which one is vital for exam preparation.

Combined or separate?

Most students take Combined Science and come away with two GCSEs; a smaller number take Biology, Chemistry and Physics separately. Both routes are catered for, with bolt-on sessions through the year.

A fun, accessible way to excel at GCSE sciences

SMARTin SCIENCE offers Y9-Y11 students a fun, accessible way to build confidence and excel in their GCSE science exams. Using a combination of engaging science education with a supportive structured approach, we make complex topics easier and help students connect with the material.

Our vision is to empower students through an enjoyable, relatable approach to science, helping them confidently advance their knowledge and exam readiness. That includes a commitment to simplifying challenging concepts and creating an environment where students feel both challenged and supported.

Four Weeks. Three sciences. One confident student.

Small group classes — enough for discussion and shared learning, small enough that nobody hides at the back. A structured, pacy, genuinely enjoyable confidence boost, built and taught by a former Head of Science.

Biology

The topics students most often confuse, organised into clear comparisons — cells, infection, organisation, homeostasis and the required practicals.

Chemistry

Atomic structure, bonding, moles and electrolysis — the periodic table's key rules, and balancing equations until it is automatic.

Physics

Energy, forces, waves and electricity — choosing the right equation, rearranging it accurately and reading the data behind it.

Exam technique

The session that improves grades fastest: command words, a structure for 6-mark questions, timed past papers and a personal revision plan.

  • Different interactive activities throughout every session
  • Short videos to watch between sessions to consolidate learning
  • Home Learning set, marked and returned – with feedback that reaches you, not just your child
  • The same four phases every week, so students always know what is coming next

See the four weeks in full → Dates & times

STEM Workshops, Afterschool Clubs and Holiday Clubs

Whether a child needs science support or simply wants to delve deeper into STEM, we provide opportunities to learn beyond the curriculum.

STEM workshops

One-off, hands-on sessions for a class, a year group or a community group — practical science with a proper question behind it.

After-school clubs

A weekly science club through term time, where the keen get stretched and the quiet ones get pulled back in.

Holiday clubs

Longer blocks in half term and the school holidays — time for the messier experiments that never fit a lesson.

See workshops & clubs →

Sessions are led by Rod Martin

Rod is a highly experienced science teacher, tutor, and former Head of Science with over two decades of teaching experience. During that time, he has watched countless bright students lose confidence in science, often because a single topic moved too quickly and left them struggling to understand what came next.

Everything parents usually ask

Y9, Y10 and Y11 students sitting GCSE Science. It suits students who are capable but have lost confidence, students who have fallen behind after missing topics, and students who understand the content but keep losing marks in exams.

Sooner than most parents expect, because the first thing that shifts is not knowledge but approach — reading the command word, showing the working, structuring a longer answer. Those habits start paying back within a few sessions and they carry into every paper afterwards.

How long the whole thing runs depends on the student. Some want a short, focused block before an exam; others keep a weekly session going through Year 10 and 11. Ask and Rod will tell you honestly what he thinks yours needs.

The core content of GCSE Combined Science is shared across AQA, Edexcel, OCR and Eduqas, and that is what the course teaches. Tell me your child's board when you enquire and the practice questions and past papers used will support it.
